verdict.line: You lose if he chains Q's slow into a level-6 Unstoppable Force before his Granite Shield has been worn down; you win by poking through the shield with your faster Q cycle and stacking poison in extended trades before his tank items come online.

brief.thesis: This matchup is structurally even — Gangplank's 48.9% win rate over 3,240 games reflects a lane where neither side has a clean mechanical answer to the other. Gangplank's faster Q cycle (5s cooldown) and level-scaling poison let him out-poke Malphite's slower 8s-cooldown Q, but Granite Shield eats a chunk of every trade until it's actively worn down. The lane tips once Malphite hits level 6: Unstoppable Force turns a passive laner into a real all-in threat, and that's the one spike window that can flip an otherwise even lane into a kill for him.

theirWindow.what: If he opens with Q's slow and follows with R's knockup, you can't dodge the hit itself, but W (Remove Scurvy) clears any lingering CC and heals you back once you land, blunting the follow-up damage window.

yourWindow.what: Shield only recharges if he avoids damage for a few seconds, so chain autos into Q (5s cooldown) back-to-back while it's down to land full damage instead of feeding the shield's absorption.

start.why: Most-picked start at 59.7% with a 48.6% win rate; the extra AD and sustain let you win the auto-trade that opens before his shield has recharged.

boots.why: Highest-winrate boots option (51.8% over 927 games); the lifesteal keeps you healthy through his Q poke and Ground Slam attack-speed reduction without needing a back.

core.why: Mana return lets you spam Q continuously against his shield-recharge window instead of running dry mid-trade.
Armor penetration cuts directly through the armor stacking that also feeds his Ground Slam's damage, keeping your Q and autos relevant into his tank build.
Crit damage scaling to burst through whatever Granite Shield is left once it's down, matching the highest-winrate core path (54.5% over 484 games).

situational.when: he stacks heavy armor and you need extra lethality to finish a low-health trade
he's committing to level-6+ all-ins off R and you need the shield to survive the knockup chain
you need the dash to dodge his Q slow and reset into another poke

runes.keystoneWhy: Triggers off the same auto-trades you're already stacking poison with, and the bonus health lets you contest and out-sustain him in lane rather than conceding it, directly per the matchup read that stacking Grasp is how you contest this lane.

summoners.why: Highest pick rate at 78.1% for a reason: Malphite has no self-healing to answer Ignite's DoT in an even lane, and Flash covers the one moment that actually threatens you — dodging or repositioning around his level-6 Q-into-R engage.

playing.title: Poke through shield gaps
playing.detail: Your Q is on a 5s cooldown against his 8s Q, so you get two pokes to his one — land them while Granite Shield is still down from a prior hit instead of into a fresh shield.

playing.title: Respect the level 6 spike
playing.detail: Track his R cooldown (120/115/110/120/120s); don't commit to extended trades right as he hits 6 until you've baited or survived one Unstoppable Force.

playing.title: Trade for poison, not burst
playing.detail: Grog-Soaked Blade applies on every hit and scales with level, so extended autoattack exchanges outvalue a single big trade that just feeds his shield.

playing.title: Shred his armor stacking
playing.detail: His Ground Slam scales off his own Armor, so he'll build tanky — prioritize Lord Dominik's Regards and The Collector from the core path to keep your damage relevant.

playing.title: Use E to extend, not just buff
playing.detail: Raise Morale's movement speed (20s cooldown, 1200 range) is best spent chasing after a landed Q or disengaging out of his Ground Slam radius, not as a pre-trade buff.

playing.title: Save R to punish, not open
playing.detail: Cannon Barrage's long cooldown and map-wide range make it a siege and punish tool for overextensions, not a reliable way to start a fight on your own.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spell rates, and win rates above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG data on the current patch (16.19.1, 3,240 Gangplank-vs-Malphite games); the trade timings, shield/cooldown interactions, and lane calls are my own tactical read of the kit, not measured stats.

stats.opponentTip: He is an easy opponent to lane against. Be careful of his (R) when he reaches level 6 while stacking up Grasp of the Undying to contest lane.
